questiontext.text:
Goal

Each competition at the Kaitoke country show records a different kind of mark. Pumpkin weights, name cards, and plain counts all appear on one board. Write one function that finds the highest mark in any competition.

Read
  • Type Parameters. Which brackets enclose a type parameter list? What type can serve as a constraint?
  • Type sets. Find the paragraphs about the tilde. How does a tilde before a type name change the set?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a bounded type parameter in angle brackets, and the method returns null when the list is empty. Java erases the type argument at compile time, so the method cannot make a T of its own. Ask what a Go type parameter still knows that an erased one does not.

static <T extends Comparable<T>> T top(List<T> xs) {
    return xs.isEmpty() ? null : Collections.max(xs);
}
Banned: any, cmp
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If the compiler says a type does not satisfy your constraint, reread Type sets and look at what sits before each type name.
  • If an empty class crashes the run, look at what your function reads before the first comparison.

Goal

The Ōhakune platform board combines timetable information from three sources. For each field, it prefers the driver's value, then the roster's value, then the printed timetable's value. An empty field does not count.

Read
  • cmp.Or. Read the signature and both documentation sentences. How many arguments can ...T accept? Which argument does the function return? What is the result if no argument qualifies?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a chain of null checks, or Optional.ofNullable(a).orElse(b) stacked twice. Neither one counts an empty string or a zero as missing, and Go has no conditional expression. One standard library call replaces the whole chain.

String p = driver != null ? driver
         : roster != null ? roster
         : timetable;
Banned: if, for, switch, len
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If the all-blank board surprises you, reread the second sentence of the doc comment and predict that case again.
  • Before you predict the last test, ask whether a one-space string equals a string's zero value.

Goal

Each fishing boat at the Kaikōura market has its own list of catches. Every stall converts a list to a different measure, but each result must remain a catch list.

Read
  • Go 1.27, Language changes. What is the first listed change? Before Go 1.27, what did the comment say Rand needed one method for?
  • Methods for organization. Compare the two chained calls. Which reads from left to right? What must you do to a generic method before calling it or converting it to a value?
  • Decoupling things. Can a generic method help a type satisfy an interface? Why?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a type parameter on the method itself, which Java has allowed since generics arrived. One rule about interfaces still differs, and the third link names that rule.

<R> List<R> map(Function<T, R> f) { ... }
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If the compiler rejects the second call in a chain, ask where the conversion function's result type is declared.
  • Reread the inside-out example at the end of Methods for organization.

testcode.text: fmt.Println(NewCatch(1, 22, 333).Map(func(n int) string { return fmt.Sprint(n) }).Map(func(s string) int { return len(s) }).Items())
lengths := NewCatch("kea", "tui", "kererū").Map[int] fmt.Println(lengths(func(s string) int { return len([]rune(s)) }).Items(), describe(NewCatch(1.5, 2.5)))

name.text: WAT 21.4: When Any Is Too Much!

questiontext.text:
Goal

A callsign is the name that a vessel uses over the radio. The harbour master at Aotea Quay logs vessel callsigns and cargo totals. Each kind of vessel builds its callsign differently, while every total keeps the unit in which it arrived. Loads arrive as plain whole counts, as the shed's own Crates, and as tonnes with a decimal part.

Read
  • When are type parameters useful? Which of the three cases covers code that would otherwise be copied for each type?
  • Don't replace interface types with type parameters. If a function only calls a method on a value, should it use an interface or a type parameter?
  • One simple guideline. Read the closing paragraph. What must you observe before using a type parameter?
Coming from Java

The reflex is to reach for a type parameter whenever more than one type turns up. Java has no operator constraints, so almost every Java type parameter carries an interface bound. Go uses the two tools for different jobs, and the article says which job each one takes.

<T extends Vessel> List<String> roll(List<T> vessels) { ... }
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Ask what each function does with one element, because one calls a method and the other applies an operator.
  • If the compiler cannot infer a type argument for an empty log, reread the second link.
